title: I Am Malala
author: Malala Yousafzai
current_text: In a report dated 10 November 2013, the All Pakistan Private Schools Federation, which says it represents more than 152,000 institutions, decided against letting pupils read I Am Malala. The book was not to be included in the schools' curriculum or stocked in school libraries.

sources.quote: The All Pakistan Private Schools Federation, which says it represents more than 152,000 institutions across the country, has decided that allowing pupils to read the book, I am Malala , would have a "negative" effect on them.
sources.title: The Independent: Private schools in Pakistan ban Malala Yousafzai's book

sources.quote: Umair Aziz & Andrew Buncombe Sunday 10 November 2013 00:00 GMT
sources.title: The Independent (date line)

sources.quote: The book will not be included in the schools' curriculum, nor will it be stocked in school libraries.
sources.title: The Independent

ban_rows.note: In Nov 2013 the All Pakistan Private Schools Federation banned the book in its member schools (The Independent, 10 Nov 2013, via Wikipedia).
Named among the ~400 titles distributed to Afghan booksellers as banned for being against 'Islamic principles and national interest'.
